title: runhmd.receipt/1
description: The runhmd receipt: a signed, shareable record that one verification happened and what it concluded. `hmd attack --receipt` issues it (bin/lib/runhmd_receipt.py), `hmd receipt verify` checks it, `/r/<id>` and `/r/<id>.json` publish it. THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE: bin/lib/runhmd_schema.py reads it at run time (no copy of these rules lives in code) and refuses any keyword it cannot enforce. The verdict vocabulary (verdict, attacks, agent, gate, regression_tests, and the id/title/severity/category of a finding) is referenced from runhmd.verdict.v1.json, never copied. WHAT A RECEIPT HOLDS: what was attacked as a content hash (subject.tree_sha256, never file contents and never a path), the verdict, each finding as a digest (sha256 of the finding's canonical JSON from the verdict document, never its counterexample text), the tool version and a UTC timestamp. It carries no secret and no counterexample text, so its exact signed bytes can be published at any visibility. SIGNATURE: Ed25519 over the bytes 'runhmd.receipt/1' LF followed by the canonical form of the receipt with its `signature` member removed. CANONICAL FORM: UTF-8 JSON with no insignificant whitespace, object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of the key, strings with the minimal RFC 8259 escapes, integral numbers written without a fraction or exponent, other numbers as the shortest decimal that round-trips (cost_usd has at most 4 and duration_s at most 2 decimal places, so no exponent form ever occurs). A receipt FILE is the canonical form of the WHOLE document (signature included) followed by one LF; a verifier rejects any other byte sequence for the same document, so the bytes served at /r/<id>.json are the bytes that were signed. `key_id` is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the raw 32-byte public key and is covered by the signature; a verifier takes the public key from a pinned trust set (--pubkey, RUNHMD_RECEIPT_PUBKEY_FILE, release/runhmd-receipt.pub), NEVER from the receipt. `signature` is the standard padded base64 of the 64 signature bytes. `verdict_sha256` is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the attested verdict document with its receipt_url member (if any) set to null: a receipt cannot hash the URL that points at it. JSON Schema cannot express cross-field rules, so `x-invariants` lists the extra rules the validator enforces; each id is implemented in bin/lib/runhmd_schema.py.

x-invariants.rule: created_at is a real UTC calendar timestamp (no 30 February, no hour 25)
the attested verdict is consistent: the runhmd.verdict/1 rules V1-V4 and G1 hold over the receipt's own verdict, attacks, findings, gates and regression_tests
cost_usd is a finite number with at most 4 decimal places and duration_s at most 2, so every implementation writes the same canonical bytes for them
